title: Source re-verification and scheme maintenance cadence documentation
context: After schemes are released, the provenance allow-list and scheme data must be kept current. A source's license can change (making the scheme's provenance incompatible), or a source's content can drift (making the scheme's mapping subtly incorrect). The maintenance cadence defines how frequently sources are re-verified, who owns each re-verification, what happens when a source becomes incompatible, and how scheme data is updated or withdrawn. Without this, the project's license discipline degrades silently over time.
objective: Write a source re-verification and scheme maintenance cadence document (docs/maintenance/cadence.md) defining: how frequently allow-listed sources are re-verified (annual minimum), who owns each re-verification, what happens if a source's license becomes incompatible (flagged by watcher-002, scheme withdrawn or rebuilt from alternative open sources), the scheme update/withdrawal process, and the overall maintenance schedule.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/maintenance/cadence.md defines the source re-verification cadence: at minimum annually, or triggered by a CHANGED result from the automated watcher-002

Document defines the re-verification process: who re-verifies (maintainer or delegate), what is checked (license text vs. stored snapshot, terms change, URL still resolves), and how the allow-list is updated

Document defines the response to a license incompatibility: scheme flagged in a tracking issue, adopters notified per data-contract.md policy, scheme rebuilt from alternative open source or withdrawn if no alternative exists

Document defines the scheme maintenance process: how mapping errors discovered post-release are triaged (severity: critical blocks next release), how corrections are versioned, and how adopters are notified
Document is owned by the maintainer/steward, reviewed annually, and linked from CONTRIBUTING.md and PLAN.md sustainability section
output: docs/maintenance/cadence.md defining source re-verification cadence, re-verification process, license-incompatibility response, scheme maintenance/withdrawal process, and ownership
